cultural.vision_reason: This is a cast copper-alloy figurative gold weight in the form of an antelope with a spiraled long horn, a classic Akan goldweight (abrammuo) type used for weighing gold dust in commerce and daily life.

physical.title: Gold Weight (abrammuo):  Antelope
physical.summary: The wealth and power of the Asante kingdom were derived primarily from its massive gold resources. Since at least 1600, small weights in brass and bronze were used to weigh gold dust and nuggets. The royal court had the most elaborate store of weights, while commoners often had about a dozen. Their imagery falls into two broad categories: geometric and representational. The latter often refers to proverbs, which used judiciously, mark a wise person. The weight in the form of an antelope with enormous horns may refer to the proverb "had I known"—a visual pun between the length of the horns and the idea of hindsight as perfect vision.

location.made_in_place: Africa, West Africa, Ghana, Akan-style artist
